patch.sql:
select
    c.customer_key,
    c.customer_name,
    c.market_segment,
    c.account_balance,
    n.nation_name,
    r.region_name
from {{ ref('stg_customers') }} c
join {{ ref('stg_nations') }} n on c.nation_key = n.nation_key
left join {{ ref('stg_regions') }} r on n.region_key = r.region_key
patch.explanation: All upstream tables have matching row counts and no missing joins. dim_customers joins stg_customers (1500 rows) with stg_nations (25) and stg_regions (5) resulting in 1319 rows, indicating some customers dropped due to join mismatches. The join to stg_nations is fine (no missing nations). Likely the join to stg_regions drops customers where region_key mismatches or region_name values not in accepted list. The code uses join on n.region_key = r.region_key, but stg_regions may have fewer rows than expected, causing loss. This is a code issue in dim_customers model.
